# BOTIA

> BOTIA reads food ingredient labels and connects what they declare with published scientific, regulatory and transparency sources — WHO, EFSA, FDA, IARC and Codex Alimentarius. It explains what a label says, what it does not say, and what cannot be concluded from it. Available in 14 languages.

BOTIA is operated by ServiceHub (Tilburg, Netherlands). It is an informational service: it does not certify food, does not give medical or nutritional advice, and does not tell anyone what to eat. Where the evidence is contested or under review, BOTIA says so.

The site is organised in two families. **Evidence layers** signal documented scientific concern. **Choice layers** support personal, ethical or religious decisions. They are kept separate on purpose.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://www.botia-safefood.com/): What BOTIA is and the four modules.
- [Evidence Layers](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/evidence.html): How BOTIA uses scientific and regulatory evidence, and what it refuses to conclude.
- [Ingredient Index](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/index.html): Searchable index of every ingredient BOTIA analyses, with its evidence layers.

## Evidence topics

- [Ultra-Processed](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/ultra_processed.html): What the NOVA classification (FAO, 2019) actually means, the four groups, and why BOTIA detects markers of ultra-processing without assigning a NOVA group to a product.
- [Hidden Sugars](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/hidden_sugars.html): Free sugars and rapidly digestible carbohydrates that can avoid the word "sugar" — including glucose syrup, fruit juice concentrate and maltodextrin — distinguishing WHO-defined free sugars from polysaccharides such as maltodextrin, which are not free sugars under the WHO definition but behave similarly once digested.
- [Honey](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/honey.html): A natural sweet substance produced by honey bees; its naturally occurring sugars are classified by WHO as free sugars, and BOTIA also flags its animal origin.
- [Not Sugar](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/not_sugar.html): Non-sugar sweeteners covered by the 2023 WHO recommendation, alongside sugar alcohols (polyols), which that guideline explicitly excludes because they are sugar derivatives that provide energy.
- [Polyglycitol Syrup](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/polyglycitol_syrup.html): E964, a hydrogenated starch-hydrolysate polyol mixture used as a sweetener and texturising ingredient.
- [The Code System](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/the_code_system.html): Why the same additive is E471 in Europe, INS 471 internationally and another name on a US label — and why the code is not the only name it appears under.
- [What Holds It Together](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/what_holds_it.html): Thickeners, stabilisers and emulsifiers — industrial function, not nutritional, and a NOVA marker.
- [Beeswax](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/beeswax.html): E901, a bee-derived wax used as a food additive for functions including glazing and texturising.
- [Tasting Like Itself](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/tasting_like_itself.html): Flavourings, including why "natural flavouring" is one of the most opaque declarations a label can carry.
- [Glutamates](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/glutamates.html): E620–E625 flavour-enhancing additives, including monosodium glutamate (MSG/E621).
- [Yeast Extract & Hydrolysed Proteins](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/yeast_extract.html): Savoury flavour-enhancing ingredients that can contain naturally occurring free glutamate even when MSG/E621 is not listed separately.

## Choice topics

- [Muslim Choice](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/muslim.html): How BOTIA classifies ingredients as halal, haram or mashbooh from what the label declares, based on Codex CAC/GL 24-1997 and OIC/SMIIC 1:2019. BOTIA is not a certification body.
- [Pork & Porcine Derivatives](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/pork.html): Pork and explicitly porcine-derived ingredients including lard, gelatine, collagen, fats, proteins, stocks and extracts.
- [Blood & Blood Derivatives](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/blood.html): Animal blood and separated blood fractions, including plasma and blood proteins such as haemoglobin.
- [Undeclared Origin](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/undeclared_origin.html): Why 72% of scanned supermarket products could not be confirmed — not because ingredients were forbidden, but because the label never declared their origin.
- [Animal Origin](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/animal.html): Ingredients that are always animal-derived, and ingredients whose origin the label leaves undeclared.
- [Milk Derivatives](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/milk_derivatives.html): Milk-derived ingredients including lactose, casein and caseinates, and whey or whey proteins.

## Health

- [Woman](https://www.botia-safefood.com/pages/woman.html): Scientific evidence relevant to pregnancy, development, reproduction or a documented difference between sexes — where such evidence exists.
- [Endocrine Disruptors](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/endocrine-disruptors.html): Cumulative exposure to substances that interfere with the hormonal system.
- [Packaging Migrants](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/packaging-migrants.html): Compounds that transfer from packaging into food and never appear on the ingredient list.
- [Fat-Soluble Accumulation](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/fat-accumulation.html): Lipophilic compounds that accumulate in fatty tissue and release during rapid fat loss, pregnancy, breastfeeding or menopause.

## About

- [Legal Notice](https://www.botia-safefood.com/legal.html): Company details, purpose of the service and its limits.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.botia-safefood.com/privacy.html): What is processed on the device, what leaves it, and which third parties are involved.

## Optional

- [Full ingredient records](https://www.botia-safefood.com/ingredients/index.html): 104 indexed ingredient records, each with what it is, why BOTIA flags it, what BOTIA cannot conclude, and its official sources.
